questions.question: You are at a restaurant and the waiter brings a dish that is clearly not what you ordered. What is the most appropriate thing to say to the waiter?
options: I think you made a mistake.
That looks terrible.
I don't like this food.
Can you take this away and give me the right one?
questions.answer: Can you take this away and give me the right one?

questions.question: A friend asks you to join them for a party at 8 PM on Saturday. You are tired and would prefer to stay in, but you want to be polite. How should you respond?
options: No, I am too tired to go out.
That sounds great, I will come.
I am not sure if I can make it.
Why are you inviting me?
questions.answer: I am not sure if I can make it.

questions.question: During a meeting, a colleague makes a suggestion that you strongly disagree with. You want to express your opinion politely but firmly. Which response is best?
options: I completely agree with you.
I think that is a very bad idea.
I see your point, but I'm not sure it will work in this situation.
You are wrong about that.
questions.answer: I see your point, but I'm not sure it will work in this situation.

questions.question: Your boss asks you to take on an extra project that will require working late. You are already very busy. What is the most professional way to respond?
options: I will do it immediately.
I can't do that, I am too busy.
I am not interested in extra work.
Maybe later, I don't know yet.
questions.answer: I can't do that, I am too busy.

questions.question: You are at a formal networking event and someone approaches you to talk about a shared interest. You want to show interest but keep the conversation open-ended. How should you reply?
options: Yes, I like it too.
That is interesting. Tell me more about it.
I don't really know much about that.
Let's talk about something else.
questions.answer: That is interesting. Tell me more about it.
